thesis: This episode argues that Robinhood is a generational winner with a strong product focus, high customer engagement, and significant long-term margin potential due to its efficient cloud-based infrastructure. It highlights Robinhood's evolution from a meme-stock platform to a sophisticated investment destination with a loyal customer base and plans for banking expansion, while also noting its competitive advantages in product velocity and regulatory reputation.

claims.claim: Robinhood is a generational winner with strong product focus and attention to detail that makes it successful.
claims.quote: At our firm, we break up the bestful universe into generational winners, which is what Robinhood would be. You've got stalwarts, which are these stable, steady-eddy companies, and then you've got opportunistic situations where it's a turnaround. That is the risk of the stalwart bucket of saying this is a really profitable monopoly and they're crushing it, which is what I'm sure people were saying

claims.claim: The speaker is a fan of Coinbase in general, but notes that Robin Hood has better product velocity.
claims.quote: I'm a fan of Coinbase in general, but if you compare Robin Hood as the only founder led brokerage left, Schwab, Fidelity, or we're talking about three to four generations, it kind of managers at this point, but Brian Armstrong is a founder. And if you look at the product velocity out of Coinbase, it just doesn't compare to Robin Hood. It does hammer home.

claims.claim: Robinhood's attention to detail and focus on product is a key competitive advantage that makes it successful.
claims.quote: The big lesson for me is that product wins. This was an industry that was very sleepy, very comfortable and very profitable. All the VCs said Robinhood, you're going to fail. Everybody that came before them that attempted something like this did fail. What they did in factoring is Robinhood's attention to detail and focus on product. Customers ultimately recognize that.

claims.claim: Robinhood's attention to detail and total empathy with the customer is what makes it successful and will continue to make them successful in the future.
claims.quote: That attention to detail and that total empathy with the customer is really what is made Robinhood successful. It will continue to make them successful in the future. Having an eye for that in a management team at a culture is super powerful. It's an incredible disruption story and one that we will continue to watch with the ambitions still being quite large.

claims.claim: Robinhood has grown up as a company with good reputation with regulators and strong influence from Dan Gallagher and Vlad.
claims.quote: Their reputation with regulators is good. Dan actually came up, I believe in 2020 or 2021. He wasn't in that 2022 hiring phase, but I think his influence has grown. Robin Hood has grown up as a company. Vlad has grown up as a company. I think the regulators recognize that as well. That's quite a time to join it. See all of the action these lip through some wars to say the least.

claims.claim: Robinhood's mobile-first approach and brand identity were key to their success, and they have demonstrated impressive product velocity.
claims.quote: It's pretty much on every product they break down the economic side and then the product experience side. And they say, we want to deliver a step change improvement on both sides.

claims.claim: Citadel is a massive market maker responsible for over 20% of total U.S. market trading on a daily basis.
claims.quote: I think Citadel trades are responsible for over 20% of total U.S. market trading on a daily basis. So they are just massive in scale.

claims.claim: Interactive Brokers has a different customer base, including small hedge funds and prop traders, which explains why they do not use payment for order flow.
claims.quote: I know everybody's payment for order flow with the exception of interactive brokers and part of that is because they've got a different customer base, small hedge funds, prop traders.

claims.claim: Schwab made the decision to go commission-free in 2019, which led to other players in the space making the same decision.
claims.quote: And then literally within weeks every other player in the space made the same decision. This ultimately crippled, for instance, TD Ameritrade, each raid, both of those ultimately got subsumed by Schwab in the one case and Morgan Stanley and the other.

claims.claim: Robinhood's customer base is not as unsophisticated as perceived, with most customers placing about 40 trades per year, similar to Schwab's average customer.
claims.quote: The real number is 40. They're placing 40 trades a year for a month, basically one a week. It's not the picture of this hyperactive day trader that you would think. Schwab's average customer, the self-directed customer trades 40 times a year.

claims.claim: Robinhood's customer base is skewed towards large cap high quality companies, with two-thirds of trades being vanilla equity, one-fourth options, and about a tenth crypto.
claims.quote: If you look at equity, it's overwhelmingly skews to large cap high quality companies. Lastly, if you think about outcomes, we know roughly 85% of day traders ultimately fail. If that was Robinhood's base, you would expect to see one, a lot of churn and then average account balances flat or probably down.

claims.claim: Robinhood is healthy with strong growth, becoming a higher mind share platform that customers want to add assets to.
claims.quote: Half net new deposits, and then it's half organic appreciation of the assets in the account. What that shows you is that investors are making good decisions. Again, these are not day traders that are blowing themselves up.

claims.claim: Robinhood is becoming a higher mind share platform that customers want to add assets to that they want to make a bigger part of their financial life.
claims.quote: Then on the other side, the really healthy net new deposits shows that Robinhood is becoming a higher mind share. It's a platform that they want to add assets to that they want to make a bigger part of their financial life.

claims.claim: Robinhood introduced crypto in 2018, while Fidelity was slower, and Schwab still hasn't launched for individual clients.
claims.quote: Robinhood introduced crypto, actually being able to buy a token itself in 2018. Fidelity was obviously slower, but in 2022, I think they launched for institutional clients, and then 2023 for individual clients, Schwab still hasn't.

claims.claim: Robinhood offers only the 10 most liquid crypto tokens, purposely holding back due to regulatory uncertainty.
claims.quote: They only offer the 10 most liquid, biggest names. If you look at a coinbase, they're offering 250. Obviously, that is their business, but Robinhood could have done the same, but purposely held back because of regulatory uncertainty.

claims.claim: 80% of customers who came during the meme-stock year are still with the company and have become real investors.
claims.quote: 80% of the customers that came on during that year are still with the company, and by all indications have become real investors. Investing, as we know, is very much a process of learning, of experimenting, and playing.

claims.claim: Robinhood is rolling out a banking offering at the end of this year, ramping up next year with high yield savings and credit cards.
claims.quote: We expect both of the sides of transaction and net interest income to scale with account growth. Robinhood is doing so many things, but at once that you have to pick what matters most. But we have followed the FinTech world for quite some time, and we think so Robinhood is rolling out a banking offering at the end of this year.

claims.claim: Robinhood banking and credit card business has potential for customers that attach to basically double RPUs, with RPU today about $150.
claims.quote: We think that is going to be very successful, specifically banking high yield savings equivalent, and then also a way credit card. We think that has the potential for customers that attach to basically double RPUs. RPU today is about $150.

claims.claim: Robinhood customers spend about two hours in the app per month, which is twice as much time as Schwab and four times as much time as Fidelity customers.
claims.quote: But if you look amongst users, Robinhood customers spend about two hours in the app per month. That's about twice as much time as Schwab. Customer is about four times as much time as fidelity customers.

claims.claim: Robinhood is giving a 3% match on IRA annual contributions, way better than anybody else in the industry.
claims.quote: They've already done this on their IRA product, which has been growing like a weed, and they are giving a 3% match on your annual contribution way better than anybody else in the industry and actually going back to kind of our original frame of Robinhood disrupting based on economics and then on product.

claims.claim: Today, 13% of users are gold customers, with a view that gold gets to 50% of penetration over time.
claims.quote: Today, 13% of users are gold customers Spotify, I think around 40% of their users are the paid tier. Our view is that gold gets to 50% of penetration over time and think about that as kind of a proxy for the savings in the banking stand.

claims.claim: The speaker believes Robinhood's business model, driven by high fixed costs and low variable costs, offers significant long-term margin potential and scalability.
claims.quote: So Robinhood is this close that they're cost structures, 85% fixed, 15% variable. The industry is actually very consolidated. Three players control 80% of the market based on accounts. You've got Fidelity Schwab and Robinhood

claims.claim: The speaker expects Robinhood's steady-state margins to be significantly higher than Schwab's due to its cloud-based infrastructure and efficiency.
claims.quote: To your point in terms of what's different, it's not being suppressed today, but I think the long-term steady state margins for Robinhood are significantly higher than Schwab. Robinhood really was born in the cloud on AWS

claims.claim: The speaker anticipates that Robinhood's margins will eventually resemble Interactive Brokers' due to cost efficiency, potentially exceeding 70%.
claims.quote: So we expect steady state, Robinhood marches to look more like interactive brokers. Interactive brokers is around 70, and their model is different, so we kind of get there for different reasons, but a lot of it is efficiency on the cost side

claims.claim: The speaker believes that tokenization could reduce transaction costs for Robinhood, pushing margins even higher than 70%.
claims.quote: Vlad has talked about a movement to real-time settlement on blockchain rails, via tokenization. Those transactions being one-tenth the cost of traditional transactions for Robinhood. So we'll see how that pans out from a regulatory perspective, but if that's true, that probably gets us even over 70%

claims.claim: The speaker notes that Robinhood's EBITDA margins are impressive, with incremental margins over the last four quarters at 81%.
claims.quote: Today, EBITDA margins are low 50s, and incrementally, but down margin over the last four quarters has been 81%. So it's really impressive. And impressive, incremental, relative to the industrials that I used to cover

claims.claim: The speaker believes that Robinhood's regulatory reputation is good, with a strong compliance team led by Dan Gallagher, a former SEC chair.
claims.quote: Their regulatory team is very strong. So Dan Gallagher runs their compliance and regulatory affairs. He was a former SEC chair and has become very much a thought leader. Vlad is even becoming a thought leader, particularly the area of tokenization

claims.claim: The speaker expects Robinhood to gain 40% incremental share of the wealth transfer, significantly increasing its asset base.
claims.quote: And that alone gets you Robin Hood today at about 300 billion assets to 4 trillion over the next decade. So just massive row that 20% versus 2% is a meaningful opportunity to start to close things down on the risk side of the equation
